items.title: 10.10 Avogadro's constant by the electrolytic method

blocks.title: Avogadro constant
blocks.text: The Avogadro constant, L, is the number of specified particles (atoms, molecules or ions) in 1 mole.

An electrolytic method can give a value for the Avogadro constant by calculating the charge associated with 1 mole of electrons: L = (charge on 1 mole of electrons) / (charge on 1 electron). The charge on the electron is found by experiment to be approximately 1.60 x 10^-19 C. The next two topics describe how the charge on a mole of electrons is found and the calculation.

blocks.prompt: Why does dividing the charge on a mole of electrons by the charge on one electron give Avogadro's constant?
blocks.explanation: A mole of electrons carries L electrons, each with charge 1.60 x 10^-19 C, so the total charge is L times the electronic charge. Measuring the total charge per mole electrolytically and dividing by the known charge per electron therefore counts the electrons in a mole, which is L.

items: L = particles per mole = (charge on 1 mol electrons) / (charge on 1 electron, 1.60 x 10^-19 C); the first is found by electrolysis.
